run.change_description: fix(vercel): Fix ISR path rewrite to prevent 404

summary.intent: Restore ISR rendering on the Vercel adapter after #15959 made `_isr` ignore the `x_astro_path` query parameter, by honouring that parameter again when the request carries `x-vercel-isr: 1`.
summary.issue_fit: Issue alignment unavailable: there is no originating issue. Intent comes from the user-supplied pull-request text (withastro/astro#16079) and the commit message. The ISR fix works in-process, but it depends on Vercel platform behaviour that cannot be checked offline.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed against merge-base b089b90 (base `main`, supplied by the caller). Traced the entrypoint, route generation in `src/index.ts`, and #15959's security test. The repository's own focused tests could not build fixtures in the read-only clone. Built scratch fixture copies instead and called `_render` and `_isr` in-process. The untracked `.mcp.json` in the clone is outside the committed range and was not reviewed.
check_details: Repository focused tests `node --test test/path-override-security.test.js test/isr.test.js` (from packages/integrations/vercel, head 71ae513): environmental failure. The fixture build hit `ENOENT: mkdir .../fixtures/<fixture>/.astro/collections/` because the clone is mounted read-only, so no assertion ran. This is not a test failure.

Reviewer run at head 71ae513: `node --test isr-header-bypass.test.js` on a work-directory copy of the `serverless-with-dynamic-routes` fixture, exit 0. The built `_render` handler returned `body.id = private` for `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` with `x-vercel-isr: 1`, and `body.id = public` without the header.

Reviewer run at head 71ae513: `node --test isr-entry.test.js` on a work-directory copy of the `isr` fixture, exit 0. `_isr` returned 200 for `/_isr?x_astro_path=/one` with `x-vercel-isr: 1` and 404 without it. The prerender config was unchanged (`allowQuery: ["x_astro_path"], passQuery: true`).

questions.title: Does Vercel strip a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` header before it reaches the function?
questions.evidence: At head, `entrypoint.ts` applies the `x_astro_path` query value as the pathname whenever `x-vercel-isr` is `1`. Nothing authenticates that header. #15959 had restricted overrides to requests carrying the middleware secret. The same bundle backs `_render` and `_isr`. In-process, `_render` rendered `/api/private` for a request to `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` that carried the header. Nothing in the repository says whether Vercel removes or overwrites this header on client requests, or whether it always sets it on ISR invocations.
questions.why_it_matters: If clients can send the header through, any visitor can pick which route `_render` or `_isr` renders. That reopens the override #15959 closed and makes this a must-fix security finding. If Vercel strips the header and sets it only on ISR invocations, the change is safe and the ISR 404 fix holds.
questions.answer: A Vercel maintainer, Vercel's documentation, or a test on a real deployment needs to say whether a client-sent `x-vercel-isr: 1` reaches `_render` or `_isr` unchanged, and whether Vercel sets the header on every ISR invocation. If the client header passes through, this candidate reopens as a must-fix finding.

observations.fact: `path-override-security.test.js` sends no `x-vercel-isr` header, so it passes at head even though `_render` now honours the query override when that header is present.

requirements.evidence: In-process, `_isr` returns 200 for `/_isr?x_astro_path=/one` with `x-vercel-isr: 1` and 404 without it. Whether Vercel sends that header on real ISR invocations is platform behaviour that was unavailable offline. If it does not, ISR routes still return 404. Question vercel-entrypoint/isr-header-trusts-client-path-override settles this.
